item.content: When validating integer inputs, reject bool explicitly (isinstance(x, bool)) since bool is a subclass of int in Python; also reject non-int types and non-positive values before using the value.

Don't assume to_money/round_money accept arbitrary input silently; verify how the money helper handles floats, NaN, and strings, and rely on its existing error codes (e.g. float_amount) rather than duplicating validation.

State transitions in ledgerly are guarded by checking invoice.status against the literal 'draft' and raising BillingError('invalid_state', ...) with the invoice id and status; follow the same pattern for any new mutating operation.
